_source: Row counts measured by Plan 103-01 on 2026-07-31 from a candidate built offline by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at v2.7-20-g7f121cc, and reconciled model-by-model against production. The classified difference table is in Plan 103-01's evidence. Re-pinned 2026-09-05 by Plan 133-02 from ONE candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at 7cea049 (66,492 rows across 70 models): eleven counts moved and every one was read off that build's manifest, not predicted. The plan named five; the build moved eleven, which is the second time in this milestone a prediction came in short (132-01 named six and moved seven). Re-pinned again 2026-09-05 by Plan 134-01 from ONE candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at d084d20 (66,504 rows across 70 models): exactly ONE count moved, surface.DiversionRecord 161 -> 173, and it was read off that build's manifest. Every other pin -- parcels.ParcelLedger at 2313 included -- reproduced unchanged, which is the proof that the storm reached no parcel's account. Re-pinned again 2026-09-06 by Plan 136-02 from ONE candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at 0e494c0 (66,505 rows across 70 models): exactly ONE count moved, surface.WaterRight 6 -> 7, read off that build's manifest; the per-GSA allocation re-size in the same plan changed amounts on 6 of the 16 accounting.AllocationPlan rows and moved no count. Re-pinned again 2026-09-24 by Plan 148-02 from ONE candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at 7950c81 (66,316 rows across 121 models): four counts moved, every one read off that build's manifest. The plan named three (WaterCredit, ParcelLedger, AllocationCarryover); surface.UnallocatedDelivery 18 -> 39 was named in the 148-02 carry-forward before the build and its cause read off the candidate (the Stevinson center pivots' lower cap). Re-pinned 2026-10-27 by Plan 151.4-02 from ONE candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh on the 151.4-02 tree (66,538 rows across 119 models), beside a candidate built the same way at 8f31bc8 that reproduced every earlier pin: six counts moved, every one read off the two manifests.
notes: Per-model row counts a rebuilt candidate MUST produce before it may become the golden snapshot.

WHY EVERY TOLERANCE IS ZERO. The rebuild makes no network calls and contains no randomness: parcels come from the committed data/merced/selected_parcels.geojson, flowlines from the committed data/merced/flowlines.json, and evapotranspiration from the committed data/merced/openet_cache.json. The same tree therefore has to produce the same numbers every time. A count that moves is not variance -- it is a change somebody made, and this gate's job is to make them say so in writing before it ships. A non-zero tolerance would have to name what varies and why; nothing here qualifies, so nothing here has one.

WHY NOT '> 0'. A check that only asserts not-zero passes a demonstration that quietly lost ninety percent of its rows and still renders every page. That is the precise failure this file exists to catch, so the comparison is equality against a written-down number.

SHAPE IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN. Production and staging once differed in only seven tables by COUNT while three tables held identical counts and completely different names. This is gate 2 of four; gates 1 and 4 read content.
WHEN A SEED CHANGE FAILS THIS GATE: that is the design, not a bug. Update the entry, change the reason to say what moved and why, and commit both together with the seed change.

off_by_default_apps.reason: The candidate is built with OPENH2O_MODULES empty, which means the default module set, and since 2026-10-12 that set leaves reporting out (core/modules.py on_by_default=False). Its models are absent from a default build, and the live site runs the same default, so its migration fingerprint has to match a golden built without them. A model of an app listed here may be absent; when it is present its count is still checked. tests/test_expected_shape.py keeps this list equal to the registry's off-by-default modules.

Earlier history: MOVED 4 -> 8 by Plan 150.3-01, read off the candidate built at c4ab970 on the staging host 2026-10-12 (gate 2 refused it, the first rebuild since that plan) and equal to staging's count: the nine points of diversion gained a lining, which sets each one's seepage share, and seepage goes to the zone's conveyance_seepage_pool, one row per GSA zone per water year (2 x 2 = 4 new rows, 5,506.73 AF in all, the seepage figure 150.3-01 recorded). The four basin_recharge_pool rows are unchanged. Earlier history: MOVED 8 -> 4 by Plan 148-02, read off ONE candidate built at 7950c81 (66,316 rows across 121 models): the four incidental_recharge_pool rows (2 GSA zones x 2 water years) are gone because an over-delivery is nobody's credit (the Q1 ruling): the engine no longer deposits canal water beyond a month's use to the basin pool. The four basin_recharge_pool rows from managed recharge events remain. Earlier history: Recharge POOL rows plus the account carryover seed_merced's allocation step writes. MOVED 4 -> 8 by Plan 133-02, observed on the candidate: 2 GSA zones x 2 pool origins (basin_recharge_pool from seed_merced_recharge_events, incidental_recharge_pool from the engine) x 2 WATER YEARS. The second water year is what is new -- a pool is keyed by water_year, so once WY 2025-2026 carries managed and incidental recharge it earns its own row per zone per origin rather than adding into the first year's.

Before that: MOVED 1824 -> 1717 by Plan 153-05 (2026-11-12), read off a candidate built by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh from the working tree: both water years now carry the crop ET OpenET sent (data/merced/openet_cache.json, received 2026-11-12), and OpenET sent no crop ET for 61 use areas in December 2025 and 46 in January 2026, so the engine writes no month for those 107 use-area months (76 x 24 = 1,824, less 107). Nothing is filled in for them (ruling 140). Before that: MOVED 912 -> 1824 by Plan 133-01, which gave the engine a second water year to calculate; that year's crop ET was generated from the first, and 153-05 replaced it with OpenET's. A candidate with 0 here has data but no accounting; a candidate with 912 has only half the demonstration and its period selector shows an empty year.

core.User.reason: THE POINT OF THE WHOLE MILESTONE. The rebuild never boots a serving web container, so entrypoint.sh's no-argument branch -- and with it ensure_superuser -- never runs. A non-zero count means a deployment's admin account got baked into an artifact that ships to production. That is the exact mechanism by which staging admin rows once reached production, and it is why every step of rebuild-golden.sh is 'run --rm' rather than 'up web'. Production's own admin returns from its .env on the next container boot after a restore, so nothing is lost by shipping zero.

datasync.DataRecordStaging.reason: The demonstration's frozen telemetry: two water years (2024-10-01 onward) for the 42 active stations, loaded from data/merced/readings.json by load_reading_fixture. The count is the generator's own output: dump_reading_fixture keeps the last real reading of each (station, parameter, statistic, calendar day), and two consecutive dumps of the same database are byte-identical. 30,951 = the 30,217 readings frozen on 2026-08-01 (USGS water temperature stored as the daily high, statistic 00001, and discharge as the daily average, 00003) plus 734 USGS daily average water temperatures (00003) fetched from the USGS Water Data APIs on 2026-11-01 for the same days: 665 at 11261500 and 69 at 11273400, where USGS publishes the average only from 2026-05-25 within these dates. Tolerance stays 0 because nothing here is sampled or random: if this number moves, the fixture was regenerated and that is a change somebody made.

datasync.DataSource.reason: Reference data: the external data sources the platform knows how to pull from, plus Entered by hand (code manual), the source of stations whose readings a person types on the station's page. Definitions, not fetched records.

datasync.TypedReading.reason: The record of who typed each reading at a station entered by hand. Zero because the demonstration has no such station.

datasync.TypedReadingEvent.reason: Change history of TypedReading. Zero because the demonstration types no readings.

datasync.DataSyncLog.reason: One row per sync pull performed. Zero because the build performs none.

datasync.MonitoredStation.reason: Frozen into data/merced/stations.json and loaded by load_station_fixture, for the same reason data/merced/flowlines.json is frozen: a gate that reddens because an upstream catalogue had a bad afternoon is a gate people learn to ignore. The demonstration's own about page lists these stations under 'Real published records -- USGS and CDEC', beside the river network, so they are demonstration content and not somebody else's registry passing through. 335 total, 42 of them is_active -- and 42 is the number the landing-page hero displays. Tolerance 0 is correct precisely because the count cannot move unless data/merced/stations.json moves. Supersedes the 103-01 reasoning that stations need not be frozen because no later seed step reads MonitoredStation: that judged them by what the build consumes rather than by what the demonstration shows.

datasync.OpenETCache.reason: 76 parcels x 5 variables x 2 WINDOWS (WY 2024-25 and WY 2025-26), loaded from the committed data/merced/openet_cache.json by load_openet_fixture. Every row is a figure OpenET (crop ET and its spread) or gridMET (rainfall) sent, received 2026-11-12 through Google Earth Engine, and carries that day and its source (Plan 153-05, rulings 139 and 140). Plan 153-06 added to each WY 2025-26 crop ET row the months Earth Engine had none for (107 use-area months in December 2025 and January 2026), as OpenET's own service sent them the same day (ruling 146); the row count did not move. The row count did not move when 153-05 replaced the second window, which until then was generated from the first. check_cache_duplication reads green with exact_duplicate_groups 0 and overlapping_span_pairs 0. Without these rows the accounting engine has no demand side and every calculation run comes out empty.

datasync.CropETFigure.reason: MOVED 1717 -> 1824 by Plan 153-06 (2026-11-12), read off a candidate built from the working tree: 76 use areas x 24 months (Oct 2024 to Sep 2026), every one recorded. The 107 months Earth Engine had no figure for (61 in December 2025, 46 in January 2026) carry the figure OpenET's own service sent, received 2026-11-12 (ruling 146); nothing is filled in by OpenH2O. Before that: OpenET's crop ET recorded once per use area and month by load_openet_fixture, at the figure and the day the file says it was received (2026-11-12). MOVED 1824 -> 1717 by Plan 153-05, read off a candidate built from the working tree: 76 use areas x 24 months (Oct 2024 to Sep 2026), less the 107 use-area months OpenET sent no crop ET for (61 in December 2025, 46 in January 2026). Those months have no record and are never filled in (ruling 140).

measurements.MeterReading.reason: Monthly totalizer reads on the 12 certified meters across BOTH water years (12 x 24), written by seed_merced_measurements. MOVED 144 -> 288 by Plan 133-02: a totalizer is a lifetime counter and does not restart on October 1, so the second year continues the first year's running value rather than opening a new record. Each month's delta is READ OFF the ParcelLedger meter_reading rows for the parcels that well irrigates, not invented -- so this number moves only if the meter set or the ledger's month coverage moves, and a change in one without the other is the regression to look for. read_by is NULL on every row: gate 2 requires core.User = 0.

measurements.Sensor.reason: One pressure transducer, on MER-W-004 -- the single monitoring well whose own declaration reads 'Continuous' (transducer logs daily). A second row means a sensor was added to a well that did not declare one.

measurements.SensorMeasurement.reason: One logged reading a day across BOTH water years (2024-10-01..2026-09-30) from the single transducer. MOVED 365 -> 730 by Plan 133-02. DAILY IS STILL THE CEILING, not a starting point: PROJECT.md puts real-time telemetry out of scope, so this is a logger downloaded on a field round. A count above 730 means something began polling; 365 means the record stops a year before the demonstration's open water year does.

measurements.WaterMeasurement.reason: Hand-entered depth-to-water readings at the cadence each monitoring well declares, across BOTH water years. MOVED 20 -> 40 by Plan 133-02 -- the same cadence, twice the span. Per year: MER-W-001 monthly (12), MER-W-002 quarterly (4), and 4 quarterly steel-tape checks against the transducer on MER-W-004. The checks sit a few hundredths off the logger on purpose -- that disagreement is what the quality flag exists to carry. recorded_by is NULL on every row.

parcels.ParcelLedger.reason: MOVED 2015 -> 2033 by Plan 153-06 (2026-11-12), read off a candidate built from the working tree and compared month by month with staging (2,015, built from the 153-05 file): +9 calculated groundwater rows in December 2025 and +9 in January 2026, the use areas that now have OpenET's figure for those months (ruling 146). No other month's count moved. In the same two months the seed's invented canal deliveries and meter readings now follow the calculation runs instead of the seed's flat fallback, so their sums moved (December deliveries -112.53 to -93.37 AF, January deliveries -135.29 to -202.69 AF, January meter readings -31.45 to -74.70 AF) with their row counts unchanged; every other month's count and sum are equal to 0.0001 AF. Before that: MOVED 2033 -> 2015 by Plan 153-05 (2026-11-12), read off a candidate built from the working tree and broken down on a build of the same file: both water years now carry the crop ET OpenET sent. In WY 2025-26, 18 calculated groundwater rows are gone (9 in December 2025, 9 in January 2026: use areas OpenET sent no crop ET for, so the engine calculates nothing there), and in February 2026 two field-months that had a meter_reading row now have a calculated row instead (2 - 2). WY 2024-25 did not move. Before that: MOVED 2148 -> 2033 when OpenH2O stopped estimating a canal delivery from crop need (2026-10-27). Reasoned, not yet read off a rebuild: the 23 estimated months of the Atwater Canal Headgate each divided their water among its 5 fields, 23 x 5 = 115 surface_diversion rows that are no longer written, and 2148 - 115 = 2033. The groundwater (calculated) rows do not move: the estimate was never subtracted from a groundwater charge. Before that: MOVED 2080 -> 2148 by Plan 151.4-02, read off the candidate built on its tree: 68 more surface_diversion rows (1,208 -> 1,276), because a headgate now divides its water by the shares entered, or by acreage, and writes a row for every field it serves; among the groundwater rows, 68 field-months now carry a 0 AF share of their well's meter reading (53 that held a seeded metered row and 15 that held a calculated estimate), offset one for one, so meter_reading 339 -> 354 and calculated 357 -> 342. Earlier history: MOVED 2085 -> 2080 by Plan 149-02, read off ONE candidate built from 72989a0 plus the seed's unmetered ditch (66,436 rows across 124 models): minus 5 split rows, the five fields of MER-POD-004-DEMO Atwater Canal Headgate in December 2024. That ditch now has no meter (2026-10-06), its delivery is estimated from its fields' crop water use, and in December 2024 the fields used none, so no delivery was estimated and nothing was divided; the typed record it replaced (2.2553 AF) had been divided five ways. Before that: MOVED 2313 -> 2085 by Plan 148-02, read off ONE candidate built at 7950c81 (66,316 rows across 121 models): minus 228, exactly the incidental recharge rows ('Credit for canal water delivered beyond the use area's estimated use for the month') the engine used to write on well fields; an over-delivery is now recorded on the CalculationRun as over_delivery_af and nowhere in the ledger (Q1). No other ledger row count moved. Earlier history: The keyed water ledger entries the accounting engine writes per parcel per period. MOVED 1271 -> 2313 by Plan 133-02, which gave the open water year its supply side. Observed composition: 176 allocation rows (88 a period -- BOTH periods always had these), 1,095 rows for WY 2024-2025 and 1,042 for WY 2025-2026. THE COMMITTED YEAR DID NOT MOVE: 1271 - 176 = 1095, exactly what it still holds. The open year's 1,042 are 588 surface_diversion, 215 calculated, 133 meter_reading and 106 recharge.
